notes.title: Investigate your neighbours in The Occupation devs' new mystery
notes.notes:
After snooping around offices in The Occupation and memories in Ether One, developers White Paper Games will soon offer the opportunity to snoop around a neighbourhood . During E3 they announced Conway: Disappearance At Dahlia View, where we'll play a former detective in 1950s England who falls into spying on his neighbours after the disappearance of a young girl. The announcement trailer remind me a bit of Hitchcock's Rear Window, spying on people out his flat window. Have a look for yourself below.

notes.title: The Occupation receives a major update including a Chapter Select feature
notes.notes:
Since the launch of The Occupation on March 5th, the White Paper team has been hard at work listening to player feedback to improve the gameplay experience. On launch, The Occupation was praised for its innovation and gameplay however was hindered by the bugs which is something we wanted to work hard to improve for our player’s experience. With this major update, we’ve included a number of features and bug fixes in response to the feedback we received.

[h1]New Chapter Select Feature[/h1]
We wanted to make sure we listened to the community and addressed all the issues. We then went to work after listening to the number one requested feature since launch - the ability to replay a chapter of the game. We’re proud to say, this feature now exists and is accessible after completing the game. 

A video of the update can be found here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JiFMP_Bz84c&feature=youtu.be
The rest of the patch notes can be found on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/765880/discussions/0/1643167006286011662/]the forum[/url] which include 5 new quality of life improvements along with 12 bug fixes. So far we've seen a really positive response so we want to thank the community for their continual support. The team have worked incredibly hard on the stability of this patch with a lot of long days so if you've been waiting to jump in, now's the time whilst it's 20% off!

Thanks again for the incredible support - we'll continue to listen to feedback to make The Occupation the best game it can be!

Thank you from the whole team!

notes.title: Patch Notes 1.2.0
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31400775/8f1e317b19b6d4194692a509207dd0a9d3e6611a.png[/img]

[h1]Hey all![/h1]

We've been working hard on fixing any issues that have arisen since launch and we're incredibly happy with this latest patch 1.2.0!

The patch includes:
[b][1][/b] Greatly improved stability of AI characters.
[b][2][/b] Fixed an issue which made AI characters leave floating objects behind.
[b][3][/b] Fixed interaction issue with briefcase which could cause you to lose items (swapping floppy disks in the pockets)
[b][4][/b] Fixed a large number of level based issues in all levels: collision issues, traversal issues, lighting and art issues, etc.
[b][5][/b] Fixed issue where collected Vinyls do not appear at the end of the game in Harvey's apartment.
[b][6][/b] Added a message in the final Harvey Apartment level to clarify the purpose of the level.
[b][7][/b] Fixed an issue with reel swapping and the RAU's that could cause the player to lose/lock a reel.
[b][8][/b] Fixed an issue where keys bound to screen lock, dossier, pager, watch and pause game all prevent the actual key from being passed through to the keyboard if it's bound to 0-9.
[b][9][/b] Fixed an issue where keypads only show 3 digits when used by AI.
[b][10][/b] Fixed an issue with 'Cloak and Swagger' - you can now restart a level if you're spotted and still unlock it with that savefile.
[b][11][/b] Fixed interaction with folded notes where prompts appeared backwards.

We're constantly checking the forums so if you spot any issues please do let us know and we'll be sure to take a look! In the mean time we'll be working on the next update. 

Thank you!

- The White Paper Team

notes.title: Patch 1.0.1
notes.notes:
[h1]Steve just got the fix he needed to be able to keep his job as a security guard before his big role in Hollywood![/h1]

The patch notes include:
[b][1][/b] Fixed an issue with Steve handing you your ID card in The Carson Offices.
[b][2][/b] You could lose the Silhouette Disk when swapping it with the eraser in the introductory level.
[b][3][/b] Player could get locked into the chair in the last level, forcing them to restart the level.
[b][4][/b] Fixed a player path issue in Metacentre from 2nd floor stock room to balcony, player can now climb out
[b][5][/b] Large fix to NPC navigation issues which caused AI to pass through walls and get stuck in various places in The Carson Office, The Metacentre and The Bowman Building.
[b][6][/b] On screen prompts when playing in Russian exceeded the bounds of the screen at some points.
[b][7][/b] Steve's presence was too strong in the Bowman Building. This has been toned down
[b][8][/b] Added additional clue in The Bowman Building to reinforce last gameplay objective
[b][9][/b] Silhouette Disk can disappear when you are taking it out of a pneumatic canister in the IPA
[b][10][/b] 4k resolution on consoles had a cursor offset during inspect mode.
[b][11][/b] Carla was only doing Coffee animations in her meeting, she now does a full host of animations as intended.
[b][12][/b] Submitted a fix for 4k and odd resolutions causing issues on PC.
[b][13][/b] Player could get locked in the room behind Charles Bowman's office. This has now been fixed.
[b][14][/b] Following certain steps, the player couldn't trigger the set piece after the IPA building level. This has been addressed.
[b][15][/b] In the final level, the meeting could get stuck and not progress after dialogue stopping. We believe we have fixed this issue with this patch, however would love player feedback to make sure it's a secure fix.
[b][16][/b] Fixes to Motion Blur and Ambient Occlusion options in menu pause menu

We hope these fixes help to address any frustration we've read about or watched over the last few days. Creating The Occupation has been a massive achievement for our team & if you've been holding off on starting your investigation until the weekend, please do let us know what you think!

Thank you so much to everyone for such an incredible release week!

notes.title: Podcast: Our proudest gaming achievements
notes.notes:
Life is hard and so are videogames. So when you do a tough thing, take pride. It doesn t matter if it seems like a small step for other people, if it s a big step for you, go ahead and puff your chest out. But do it quickly, for heaven s sake. We ve only got an hour. notes.title: Wot I Think: The Occupation
notes.notes:
Developer: White Paper Games
Publisher: Humble Bundle

Release: Out now
On: Windows
From: Steam, Humble, GOG
For: 20, $30, 30

The Occupation is a game easily described as flawed but interesting , which I do agree with, but then you wouldn t appreciate it if a friend said the same thing about your homemade lasagne, would you?

I didn t technically finish playing The Occupation, because in the final cutscene I didn t get the pivotal dialogue option. The characters, who I was supposed to be choosing sides between, just stared at me, unblinkingly, like two ideologically opposed owls. I wasn t even narked that it bugged out. Do I pick the right wing anti-immigration capitalist pigdog with bad glasses, or the left wing bleeding heart who is also a terrorist? Classic. Who can be bothered?

Flaws, yes, flaws a-plenty. But up until I was forced into a mixture of industrial and regular espionage, I was having some of the best fun I ve had in a game for ages.

notes.title: The Occupation sneaks into stores in search of a scoop
notes.notes:
The Occupation is out now, White Paper Games’s investigative journo-thriller wrapped in the trappings of a sneaky immersive sim. Putting players in the shoes of an English journalist in 1987, a restrictive government bill that sounds remarkably like the American PATRIOT act is about to come into force. There’s only a few hours left, and the clock is ticking in real-time, but snooping around the right places might provide the evidence to derail the government’s plans. So far, responses to the game’s launch have been all over the place, but I can’t deny the launch trailer below looks rather striking.

notes.title: The Occupation review - a brilliant, if broken, British BioShock
notes.notes:
If this review was nowt but swear words - and by that, I mean just an endless rant of disgusting words glued end-to-end ad infinitum - I still wouldn't be able to properly convey how much The Occupation frustrates me.

Because the worst thing about this - the most egregious thing, the most toe-curlingly infuriating part of it - is that I love The Occupation. I love its premise and art style. I love its killer 80s soundtrack and novel real-time conceit. It truly has some of the finest voice-acting I've heard for a while. But it is also broken, glitchy, buggy, and nonsensical, and for every one thing that colours me impressed, another five makes me scream at the screen in frustration - usually when the game bugs out completely, taking an hour's worth of my progress with it.

The premise of The Occupation is that you control the narrative. As the journalist Harvey Miller, you explore your environments, scavenging for leads and collecting evidence. Consequently, you control how you conduct your interviews with the people of interest, and any additional evidence you uncover can be used to surprise your witnesses. You get to decide whether you sit politely and await your appointed time or whether - when the security guard's back is turned - you slip silently into the Staff Only section to do a little digging. Turns out everyone has a slightly different version of events, and it's up to you to discern which account is truthful.

notes.title: The anatomy of a scoop in journo-thriller The Occupation
notes.notes:
As a lifelong fan of immersive sims since before we had a name for the genre, I need to get my grubby mitts on The Occupation, an investigative thriller set in politically taut ’80s London. With a clock ticking in real-time and a conspiracy to be untraveled before a quiet and painfully legal government crackdown, there’s a lot to be done. With only days until it launches on March 5th, developers White Paper Games have released ten minutes of footage, showing us how a single lead can be followed in order to catch a conspirator in a lie. notes.title: First-person investigator The Occupation delayed into 2019
notes.notes:
I’ve been keen to get stuck into The Occupation next week, investigating an apparent terrorist attack in 1987 England by snooping and interviewing people across simulated real time, but alas I’ll have to wait. The Occupation had been due next Tuesday, October 9th, but developers White Paper Games today announced a short-notice delay pushing it all the way back to February 5th, 2019. They give the usual reason: they want more time to make it proper good, yeah? Which I’m certainly okay with. I’d rather play a better version of the game later than a so-so one now.

notes.title: Investigative thriller The Occupation breaks its story October 9th
notes.notes:
First-person thriller The Occupation (from Ether One devs White Paper Games) looks like an exciting spin on the immersive sim genre. Playing as a journalist in 1987 England, there’s sneaking, talking and even a bit of Deus Ex-ish crawling through vents to be done in search of the truth behind a (presumed) terrorist bombing. Unlike most games, the entire story plays out over the course of four real-time hours. Either you get to the truth and make your choices by then, or the government will pass a restrictive new set of laws unopposed. Unveiled last year, the game now has a release date set – this October 9th.
